findings.claim: The new --shout flag has no test: tests/greet_test.sh still checks only the plain greeting, so breaking the uppercasing or the flag parsing would leave the suite green.
findings.suggestion: Add an end-to-end check through the command, next to the existing one in tests/greet_test.sh, e.g. [ "$(sh "$(dirname "$0")/../bin/greet.sh" --shout ada)" = "HELLO ADA" ]. Consider also --shout with no name (expect HELLO WORLD), which covers the shift leaving no argument.

findings.claim: Switching the output from printf to echo changed behaviour for names with backslashes ('a\tb' now prints a real tab under /bin/sh), and no test pins the literal output, so this went unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Keep printf '%s\n' "${line}" for the output, and add a test that a name holding a backslash is printed as written.

noticed.text: tr a-z A-Z only uppercases ASCII letters (shellcheck SC2018/SC2019, info); a name like 'élan' stays partly lowercase. [:lower:] [:upper:] would follow the locale.
The comment says --shout 'first prints it in capitals', which reads as if it prints twice; it prints the greeting once, in capitals.
The README doesn't mention the new --shout flag.

notes.text: The existing test still passes with the change (sh tests/run.sh: all passed), and the default greeting is unchanged.
The flag check sits on the left of &&, so set -e doesn't abort when the flag is absent, and ${1-} keeps set -u safe with no arguments.
